smell: One of two near-identical blocks in `findOrDownloadFCOSISO` still does `slices.Sort(matches); matches[len(matches)-1]` to fetch the lexicographically-largest filename. The sibling block at lines 57-61 was already rewritten to `slices.Max(matches)`; this one (lines 70-74) was left behind. `slices.Max` returns exactly that value in one call without mutating the input.
fix_summary: Replace `slices.Sort(matches); isoPath := matches[len(matches)-1]` with `isoPath := slices.Max(matches)`. Go 1.21+. Drops 2 lines and removes the mutation of `matches`. Apply the same rewrite the sibling block at lines 57-61 already has.
must_preserve: Newest-by-lexicographic-version selection. `slices.Max` on `[]string` uses lexicographic ordering, so the selection is unchanged. Guard the nonempty precondition (`len(matches) > 0`) — `slices.Max` panics on empty.

smell: `for _, line := range strings.Split(strings.TrimSpace(coRaw), "\n")` materializes the split slice only to walk it. Go 1.24's `strings.Lines` iterator skips the allocation. Four sibling call sites flagged in the prior run landed; this one (cli/status.go) and four newly discovered sites (layouts.go:41, tools.go:217, checksum.go:83, flux/flux.go:285) remain.
fix_summary:
Replace `for _, line := range strings.Split(s, "
")` with `for line := range strings.Lines(s)`. Go 1.24 stdlib, no import change. `strings.Lines` keeps the trailing '
' on each yielded segment — sites that don't already trim must add a `strings.TrimRight(line, "
")` or `strings.TrimSpace`. Sites: status.go:171 (TrimSpace at the source, safe), layouts.go:41 (materialized slice also walked later — keep Split there or walk twice with Lines), tools.go:217 (just reads [0] — use `strings.Cut` on the TrimSpace'd string), checksum.go:83, flux.go:285.
must_preserve: Per-site semantics (blank/comment skipping, first-line-only reads, TrimSpace normalization). For layouts.go:41 the `lines` slice is used in two places — the swap to Lines needs both loops to adapt, or leave as Split there.

smell: `append(append([]string{}, m.queryArgs...), pkg)` nests two `append`s to clone-then-extend a slice. Go 1.22's `slices.Concat` expresses the same intent in one call and also matches the repo's existing `slices.Concat(a, b)` style (see internal/cli/helpers.go:213, internal/distribution/okd/dns/dnsmasq.go:155).
fix_summary: Replace with `args := slices.Concat(m.queryArgs, []string{pkg})`. Requires `slices` import (not currently imported in this file — the sibling InstallPackages uses a plain `append([]string{...}, installed...)` which is already idiomatic). One line, no double-allocation, no nested-call cognitive load.
must_preserve: Clone-semantics — the returned slice does NOT alias `m.queryArgs`, so a downstream mutation is safe. slices.Concat always returns a fresh allocation.

smell: `statusNode.role()` iterates every key of `Labels` to check for two specific well-known strings. This is a map lookup dressed as a scan — O(n) in label count when a direct `if _, ok := Labels["node-role.kubernetes.io/master"]; ok` is O(1) and reads straight.
severity_reason: ad-hoc severity: the loop masks a straightforward map-index check — downstream readers have to trace the loop to see it is really a membership test, and the O(n) walk runs once per node in the status summary
fix_summary: Replace with direct map index: `if _, ok := n.Metadata.Labels["node-role.kubernetes.io/master"]; ok { return "master" }; if _, ok := n.Metadata.Labels["node-role.kubernetes.io/worker"]; ok { return "worker" }; return "unknown"`. No imports needed. Same semantics, O(1), 5 lines vs 11.
rule_source: Go proverb: clear is better than clever
Go spec: map element access with comma-ok
must_preserve: Master-wins-over-worker precedence when (hypothetically) a node has both labels — the current for-loop also has nondeterministic iteration order, so the current code does NOT actually guarantee master precedence. The refactor makes it explicit, which is an improvement, not a change.

smell: Two sequential `if X > innerWidth { innerWidth = X }` blocks compute a running max over two candidates. Go 1.21's `max` builtin collapses both into `innerWidth = max(innerWidth-ContentPadding+maxContentWidth+ContentPadding, minWidthForTitle)` — or more readably, `innerWidth = max(innerWidth, maxContentWidth+ContentPadding, minWidthForTitle)`.
fix_summary: Replace with `innerWidth := max(width-ContentPadding, maxContentWidth+ContentPadding, minWidthForTitle)`. `max` takes variadic ordered args in Go 1.21+. Drops 7 lines to 1 and removes the two intermediate mutations.
rule_source: Go 1.21 release notes: min/max variadic builtins
must_preserve: Result stays ≥ width-ContentPadding, ≥ maxContentWidth+ContentPadding, AND ≥ minWidthForTitle — variadic max preserves the pairwise invariants.

smell: `padding := innerWidth - lineWidth; if padding < 0 { padding = 0 }` is a hand-rolled `max(padding, 0)` — the exact floor `max` was added (Go 1.21) to express. This pattern has been flagged and fixed in at least three sibling files already; layouts.go is the last holdout in the tui package.
fix_summary: Replace with `padding := max(innerWidth-lineWidth, 0)`. Drops 3 lines to 0.
must_preserve: Non-negative padding (no negative-repeat panic on over-wide lines).
